items.title: Sonic-style platform game
items.creator: AiBattle
items.description: A fast platform-game demonstration with rings, loops and a moving character. This excerpt shows the Max version of the creator’s comparison.
items.note: Watch how movement, collectible feedback and the camera work together. An unofficial fan-game prototype.
items.prompt: Build an original 3D platform game with a fast character, collectible rings, ramps and one loop. Use your own visual identity. Add keyboard controls, score, restart and a camera that keeps the route readable. Test movement and collision before adding more levels.

items.title: Interactive Model X website
items.creator: ashe
items.description: A car model separates into pieces while the viewer selects individual components and reads their descriptions.
items.note: Existing 3D asset: cgi Moon on BlendKit. This is a visual study with illustrative internals.
items.prompt: Build an interactive product website for [PRODUCT] using my licensed 3D model. Let visitors separate its parts, select a component and read a short description. Add reassembly, orbit and reset controls. Preserve the asset credits and test it on desktop and mobile.

items.title: A furnished home you can walk through
items.creator: Thomas Ricouard
items.description: A recording moves through a furnished home, including the kitchen, living area and workspace.
items.note: The creator’s launch-demo thread describes a workflow from Blender into a walkable Unreal scene.
items.prompt: Turn my [FLOOR PLAN OR ROOM BRIEF] into a furnished 3D home. Start with the room layout, doors and windows, then add furniture, materials and lighting. Produce a walk-through with collision and a reset view. State any dimensions you had to assume.

items.title: An explorable beating heart
items.creator: Higgsfield AI
items.description: The heart keeps beating while its structures separate and labels remain visible around the model.
items.note: An educational anatomy demonstration from Higgsfield AI. The animation makes relationships between structures easier to inspect.
items.prompt: Create an educational 3D heart explorer with named structures, a beat animation and a layer-separation control. Let learners select a part and read a sourced explanation. Include reset and pause controls, cite anatomy references and clearly label illustrative simplifications.

items.title: Custom brick-model planner
items.creator: Emm
items.description: A miniature temple becomes an exploded brick model, with counts and a parts panel beside it.
items.note: The clip demonstrates model planning; physical assembly has not been tested here.
items.prompt: Create a brick-model planner for [OBJECT]. Show an assembled model, an exploded view and an editable parts list. Use a documented parts library and track colors and quantities. Identify structural assumptions and export the design for review before anyone buys the parts.

items.title: Car-soccer prototype
items.creator: am.will
items.description: Cars chase a large ball around a stadium, with boosts, goals and score feedback.
items.note: A recorded fan-game experiment inspired by Rocket League. Use it to study the game loop and camera.
items.prompt: Build an original car-soccer game in a compact stadium. Add driving, boost, ball collisions, two goals, score and round restart. Start with one player and a simple opponent. Make scoring and resets reliable, then refine the camera and vehicle handling.

items.title: Moonlit Forge: a changing 3D scene
items.creator: Guizang
items.description: A small cottage scene changes its lighting, colors and surrounding foliage as the page is explored.
items.note: The creator describes modeling, web interactions and deployment as connected stages.
items.prompt: Build a small 3D cottage website where scrolling moves through night, sunrise and changing seasons. Coordinate the model, background, lighting and short text. Include manual scene controls, a reduced-motion mode and a responsive layout. Test scrolling forward and backward.

items.title: Interactive iPhone history
items.creator: bluedev
items.description: Different phone generations appear with familiar home screens and app interfaces.
items.note: A useful example of turning a timeline into something visitors can explore. Independent interface recreation.
items.prompt: Build an interactive history website for [PRODUCT FAMILY]. Let visitors choose a year and explore a representative interface with working sample controls. Include a short change summary for each generation, accessible navigation and clear source credits. Label recreated screens as demonstrations.

items.title: Bubble-wrap playground
items.creator: FinkTheArtist
items.description: A first-person playground uses different tools to pop and break a room filled with bubble-wrap surfaces.
items.note: Watch the immediate visual feedback, tool switching and running pop counter.
items.prompt: Build a playful first-person bubble-wrap room in Three.js. Give the player three harmless virtual tools with different popping effects, a visible counter and a reset button. Add responsive controls and keep the scene smooth as many bubbles change state.

items.title: A 3D board-game prototype
items.creator: Meng To
items.description: A hexagonal board, dice, resource cards and player panels turn a tabletop-style game into an animated interface.
items.note: This is a Catan-inspired fan prototype. The creator’s post describes follow-up work on guidance and gameplay.
items.prompt: Build an original turn-based board game on a hexagonal map. Define your own resource and victory rules. Include dice or turn events, resource cards, a simple computer opponent and a help panel. Explain each action and test a complete match from setup to victory.

items.title: 3D product mockup studio
items.creator: Josh Millgate
items.description: A laptop mockup changes its presentation while controls adjust the scene and surface appearance.
items.note: Notice how a useful control panel accompanies the attractive render.
items.prompt: Build a product mockup tool for my [SCREENSHOT OR PACKAGING ART]. Place it on a licensed 3D model, then let me adjust the camera, lighting and background. Add reset and image export. Show upload errors clearly and test the exported image dimensions.

items.title: A landscape-led portfolio
items.creator: Varun
items.description: A richly illustrated landscape frames a personal portfolio’s headline, navigation and call to action.
items.note: This excerpt highlights the visual direction of the opening page.
items.prompt: Create a portfolio for [PROFESSION] using a cohesive landscape illustration as the opening scene. Make the headline, projects and contact action readable. Add subtle motion and a restrained project section. Use my supplied work and test contrast, keyboard navigation and mobile layout.

items.title: Breath Atlas lung visualization
items.creator: The Bugged Dev
items.description: A lung model changes alongside adjustable inputs and educational explanations.
items.note: Educational illustration, not a test of an individual’s lungs. Recording shared by @0xKenny1st; app credit: @thebuggeddev.
items.prompt: Build an educational lung visualization with a clearly labeled illustrative model, selectable structures and sourced explanations. Keep it separate from personal diagnosis or risk scoring. Add accessible controls and a reset view. Have a qualified reviewer check the educational content before publishing.

items.title: A train drawing becomes a Blender model
items.creator: Tom Krcha
items.description: A steam locomotive is inspected in Blender, with wireframes and individually selected objects visible.
items.note: The reference drawing remains visible, making the relationship between input and model easy to compare.
items.prompt: Use my reference drawing of [OBJECT] to build an editable Blender model. Separate meaningful parts, name the objects and keep materials organized. Show the result from several angles and compare it with the reference. Deliver the Blender file and list any missing or approximate details.

items.title: A Manhattan world in Unreal
items.creator: Matt Shumer
items.description: The recording moves from a city overview to detailed streets, buildings and a car at ground level.
items.note: The creator describes an iterative, week-long environment build. The clip shows the resulting scene.
items.prompt: Create a navigable 3D neighborhood inspired by [PLACE]. Build connected streets, varied buildings and recognizable landmarks. Add an aerial view and street-level movement. Keep scale consistent, test collisions and document which details are approximate or use existing assets.

items.title: A melody with a virtual pianist
items.creator: Leon Lin
items.description: A virtual pianist performs at a grand piano while the camera cuts between the player, keys and instrument.
items.note: Sound is retained in this excerpt. The creator credits Astra with the melody and 3D performer.
items.prompt: Compose a short original piano melody and build a simple 3D performance around it. Export the audio and note timings, animate the keys from those timings and add two clear camera angles. Render a video with synchronized sound and provide the editable project.

items.title: A music arrangement in Ableton
items.creator: Pietro Schirano
items.description: The recording shows a multi-track arrangement playing inside Ableton.
items.note: Sound is retained. The creator describes giving Astra access to Ableton through MCP to build instruments and an arrangement.
items.prompt: Using my connected music workspace, create a short original [GENRE] arrangement with separate drum, bass, harmony and melody tracks. Explain the structure, set sensible levels and export a preview. Save the editable session and identify any instruments or plugins required.

items.title: A robot paints with a real brush
items.creator: thijs
items.description: A physical robot moves a paintbrush across paper while the recording shows successive painting attempts.
items.note: The creator supplied the robot, camera and brush; Astra worked on controlling the setup.
items.prompt: Plan a supervised robot-painting demonstration for my existing [ROBOT]. First simulate brush paths and define movement limits. Show a preview for review, then use the robot’s supported control interface within those limits. Include an immediate stop control and record the result for comparison.
